questions.question: If your vehicle has a two-part safety belt system, what should you do?

options.text: Use both the lap and shoulder belts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the lap and shoulder belts.
questions.explanation: Always wear both the lap belt and shoulder belt together. Using only one part leaves you unprotected. If you have an automatic shoulder belt, buckle your lap belt as well.

questions.question: Like alcohol and other drugs, drowsiness can:

options.text: Help you be a better driver.

questions.explanation: Lack of sleep causes poor driving. Sleepiness slows your reaction time, reduces your awareness, and impairs your judgment just like alcohol and drugs do.

questions.question: When driving in fog, what should you do?

options.text: Turn on your high beam headlights.
Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
Increase your speed to avoid accidents.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: When driving in fog, slow down and use your low beam lights. If the fog is too thick to see, pull off the road safely and wait for it to clear.

questions.question: If a tire suddenly goes flat while you are driving, what should you do?

options.text: Pump the brake pedal rapidly several times.
Slow down gradually and do not brake.
Press the brake pedal down as hard as you can.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gradually and do not brake.
questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel firmly and keep the vehicle straight. Remove your foot from the accelerator and do not brake. Let the vehicle slow on its own. Use the brakes gently only if needed. Pull off the road safely when you can.

questions.question: Why should drivers give extra space to children on bicycles?

options.text: They do not have the same reflexes as adults.
They are smaller and harder to see than adults.

questions.explanation: Children are unpredictable and hard to see. Watch carefully for children near schools, bus stops, playgrounds, parks, and ice cream trucks. Be aware that children on bikes may suddenly enter the road from the sidewalk.

questions.question: After losing driving privileges for not paying crash damages, a driver must file proof of financial responsibility with the Secretary of State before regaining driving privileges.
questions.explanation: Drivers at fault in a crash without liability insurance must provide proof of payment to the Secretary of State. Failure to do this can result in a suspended license.

questions.question: You see a green light but traffic is blocking the intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Partially enter the intersection to claim your right-of-way.
Do not enter the intersection until you can drive completely across.
Continue into the intersection and wait for traffic to clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not enter the intersection until you can drive completely across.
questions.explanation: Even with a green light, only enter the intersection if you can cross it completely before the light turns red. Blocking the intersection can result in a citation.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: A round sign means a railroad crossing is ahead. This sign appears a few hundred feet before the tracks. Slow down, look, listen, and be ready to stop.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Until after you pass the sign.
Unless it seems safe to do so.

questions.explanation: A white rectangular sign shows a rule you must follow. This sign means do not pass other vehicles under any circumstances.

questions.question: Reaction time becomes slower after:
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reflexes and reaction time. It reduces your ability to see clearly and makes you less alert. As you drink more, your judgment gets worse and your driving skills decrease. You will have trouble judging distances, speeds, and how other vehicles are moving.

questions.question: A child is riding a bicycle near your vehicle. What should you do?

options.text: Expect the child to have full control of the bicycle.

questions.explanation: Children on bicycles can be unpredictable. Young cyclists may change direction suddenly. Children and bicycles are small and hard to see.

questions.question: You see pedestrians in a crosswalk ahead. What should you do?

options.text: Continue ahead. You have the right-of-way.
Wait for the pedestrians to cross the street.
Pull to the right and go around the pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for the pedestrians to cross the street.
questions.explanation: You must let pedestrians cross at a crosswalk. Wait until they have crossed before you proceed.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot make a U-turn. You cannot turn around to go in the opposite direction at this location.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Check for vehicles in your direction only, then go.
Let all vehicles that arrive before or after you go first.
Check for traffic in all directions before going.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check for traffic in all directions before going.
questions.explanation: At a stop sign, you must stop completely and look in all directions before proceeding.

questions.question: When driving through a construction zone, you should:

options.text: Stay closer to the car in front of you.
Pass carefully and do not slow down to look at unusual sights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pass carefully and do not slow down to look at unusual sights.
questions.explanation: Do not slow down to look at unusual things. This helps prevent traffic congestion.

questions.question: If you cannot merge safely into traffic, you should stop even though the sign says yield.
questions.explanation: When you must yield, you also must stop if you cannot merge safely into traffic.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign means a steep hill is coming. Slow down and shift to a lower gear to control your speed and protect your brakes.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching a construction area?

options.text: Speed up to get away quickly.
Slow down, do not use your phone, and yield to workers.
Honk your horn to alert workers to your presence.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, do not use your phone, and yield to workers.
questions.explanation: Near construction areas, you must slow down, put away your phone (unless using hands-free), yield to workers, and stay alert.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign means the road is slippery when wet. Be careful in these areas.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The right lane is ending. Move to the left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right lane is ending. Move to the left lane.
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign means one of the lanes is ending. Move to the left lane before you reach that point.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: One lane is ending. Move to the left lane.
A highway entrance ramp is coming.

questions.correctAnswerText: One lane is ending. Move to the left lane.
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign tells drivers that the right lane will end soon. You need to move left to merge with other traffic.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A school or school crosswalk is ahead.
Slow down and watch for children.

questions.explanation: This sign is placed near schools to warn drivers. You should slow down, be careful, and look for children.

questions.question: If you must make an emergency stop on an interstate, you should:

options.text: Honk your horn to get other drivers' attention.
Get out and flag down the next car that passes.
Pull off the road, turn on your emergency lights, and stay in your car if possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull off the road, turn on your emergency lights, and stay in your car if possible.
questions.explanation: If you stop on an interstate shoulder, turn on your emergency lights to warn other drivers. Stay in your vehicle if you can. Cars move very fast on interstates, so it is dangerous to stand or walk on the shoulder.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: A triangle-shaped sign pointing down means yield. Slow down to a safe speed and stop if needed. If you stop, do so at the marked stop line if one exists.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The road will be slippery ahead.

questions.explanation: This sign means a divided highway is beginning ahead. Stay to the right of the center divider.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The road is slippery when wet.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road is slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road may be slippery when wet. Drive carefully on roads with this sign.

questions.question: What is the penalty for illegally passing a stopped school bus?

options.text: Loss of driving privileges or vehicle registration, plus a $300 fine.
A $30 fine and 14 days without driving privileges.

questions.correctAnswerText: Loss of driving privileges or vehicle registration, plus a $300 fine.
questions.explanation: If convicted of passing a stopped school bus with flashing lights and the stop arm extended, you will lose your driving privileges, pay a $300 fine, and do community service set by the court. If you were not driving, the owner must report the driver's name or the vehicle registration will be suspended for three months.

questions.question: Slowing down to look at accidents or unusual things on the road:
questions.explanation: Do not slow down to stare at accidents or other things on the road. This slows traffic and causes jams.

questions.question: If your front right wheel goes off the pavement, you should ease off the gas, let the car slow down, and gently steer back onto the road.
questions.explanation: If your wheels drift off the pavement onto the shoulder, grip the wheel firmly, take your foot off the gas, and brake gently. Check for traffic behind you, then carefully steer the vehicle back onto the road.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Parking spaces for people with disabilities.

questions.correctAnswerText: Parking spaces for people with disabilities.
questions.explanation: This sign shows parking spaces reserved for people with disabilities who have special license plates or parking placards.
